paragraphs.text: Pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1) is characterized by neonatal renal salt wasting with dehydration, hypotension, hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis, even though aldosterone levels are elevated (Geller et al., 1998). The autosomal dominant or sporadic form is milder than the autosomal recessive form and remits with age (Geller et al., 1998; Viemann et al., 2001). Viemann et al. (2001) contrasted it with the autosomal recessive form, which is caused by mutations in the amiloride-sensitive sodium channel.

paragraphs.text: Armanini et al. (1985) described pseudohypoaldosteronism as a salt-wasting syndrome with failure to thrive that usually presents in infancy. Features include high urinary sodium despite hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hyperreninemia, and elevated aldosterone levels. They studied a 28-year-old index case in Melbourne (patient 1) and 2 sibs in Munich, aged 8 and 2 years (patients 2 and 3), whose parents were first cousins. Clinically, patient 3, a boy, was less severely affected than his sister.

paragraphs.text: Hanukoglu (1991) reported a kindred (kindred I) with the renal form of PHA I. The propositus presented in infancy with renal salt wasting, vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. He responded dramatically to a high-salt diet (2.5 g/day) and no longer needed sodium supplementation after age 2 years. In 7 additional members across 3 generations, clinical expression ranged from asymptomatic to moderate. In the affected members (the propositus, his mother, and 2 brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 years, but plasma renin activity (PRA) fell gradually to near normal values. The author took this to indicate tertiary hyperaldosteronism from an autonomously functioning zona glomerulosa.

paragraphs.text: In 1 sporadic and 4 dominant PHA1 kindreds, Geller et al. (1998) identified heterozygous mutations in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (MLR; NR3C2). The mutations were 2 frameshift mutations (1 of them de novo), 2 premature termination codons, and 1 splice donor mutation.
